findings.finding: The rule 'no text left in the tree says Legion refuses a merge over a check' cannot be proved by the spec's four-string search: four texts state the rule carrying none of those strings (classify/required.go:20-27, requiredchecks/requiredchecks.go:4-7, docs/site/.../legion/using-legion.md:118-120, walkthrough.md:67-68) and eleven more carry a banned string but are not on the spec's edit list.
findings.answer: Plan decision D1 and task F: the plan names every known file (F3) and replaces the four literal strings with a wider sweep set (F2) whose every hit is resolved and whose output is recorded in the pull request body. The rule is restated as: no text outside CHANGELOG.md, docs/plans/ and docs/solutions/ asserts that Legion, rather than GitHub, decides a merge on a check.

findings.finding: The spec's proof for deliverables 3 and 5 asks one test for two end states that cannot both happen: a failing required check on an accepted READY head moves the issue out of awaiting_merge (engine.go:794-795), which ends the merge row (auto_merge.go:75-82), so that row never reaches an hour and never warns.
findings.answer: Recorded as spec departure 1 and split in the plan: task A/B tests 3 and 5 separately. The warning is proven on a head that waits without being red - a required check the head has no result for, which classify.Standing.Red() excludes (classify/required.go:20-27) and which is exactly what the deleted READY_CHECKS_NOT_GREEN used to catch.

findings.finding: The one-hour warning has no contract: what starts the hour, whether a reopen restarts it, what the notice kind is called, whether it fires for a by-hand READY, and which waits count.
findings.answer: Plan decisions D2, D4, D5 and task B: the hour runs from outbox.created_at (the only durable timestamp; ReadyMerge carries no time, record/outbox.go:404-419); a reopen at the same head clears the payload flag and so warns again, a READY at a new head is a new row; the kind is merge-waiting; a by-hand READY queues no row and is out of scope (D5); every wait counts except a cause permanentRefusal already reports, which ends the row and tells the architect itself.

findings.finding: Deleting the CI line leaves the tester's duty and the simplify pass with no source: pr-body.md:98-99 ('cited from the CI line'), :127-128 ('re-cites the CI line') and prompts/roles/core/tester.md:5, none of which the spec lists.
findings.answer: Plan decision D6 and tasks C4 and D1: the duty stays and the source becomes GitHub, read at the head the role is judging, and neither role records what it read for a later step. core/tester.md:5, SKILL.md:284-291 and pi-legion/scripts/skill-scenarios/rig.sh:619 are added to the edit list.

specDepartures.spec: How it is proven, item by item: 'For the third and the fifth, a daemon test puts a failing required check on an accepted readiness head and asserts the end state it records: the issue back with its implementing agent, and a wait that tells the architect rather than one that says nothing.'
specDepartures.plan: Two tests, not one. The third deliverable keeps today's assertion (a failing required check on an accepted READY head sends the issue back to implementing and withdraws the submitted merge). The fifth is proven on a head that waits without being red: a required check the head has no result for.
specDepartures.evidence: A red on an accepted READY head leaves awaiting_merge (workflow/engine.go:794-795 calls withdrawReady on TriggerChecksRed), after which daemon/auto_merge.go:75-82's keep reads awaitedREADY, finds no awaited head, and ends the ready_merge row; the row therefore never reaches an hour and never warns. classify/required.go:20-27 shows Standing.Red() excludes Missing and Pending, so a required check with no result is the standing that actually waits.

acceptance: The proof of deliverables three and five is two daemon tests rather than one: one for the red send-back and withdrawal, one for the hour warning on a head whose required check reported nothing.

specDepartures.spec: 'a merge Legion submitted and GitHub has not completed within an hour tells the issue's architect once'
specDepartures.plan: The hour is measured from the moment the ready_merge outbox row was queued (outbox.created_at), which is READY's acceptance, not from the moment GitHub was first asked.
specDepartures.evidence: record.ReadyMerge carries Number, Head and Armed only (record/outbox.go:404-419) and nothing in the daemon records the submission time. outbox.created_at (store/migrations/0004_record.up.sql:80, record.OutboxRow.CreatedAt) is the only durable timestamp, and it survives retries, the arm-remembering write and a reopen's upsert (record/store.go:716-718 sets attempts, payload and lease_token only). The first attempt runs within seconds of the queue, so the two differ only when a GitHub rate limit defers the row.

acceptance: The warning fires an hour after the merge row was queued at READY's acceptance, not an hour after the first submission to GitHub.

specDepartures.spec: 'Fifth, a merge that waits is bounded and said out loud.'
specDepartures.plan: Every merge Legion submits is bounded. A READY a person merges by hand gains no bound, and the plan says so as a non-goal.
specDepartures.evidence: workflow/ready.go:36-41 returns before enqueuing when the merger's MergeNote is set, so a by-hand READY has no ready_merge row to warn about; workflow/ready_test.go:74 asserts that absence, and daemon/auto_merge.go:164-171's awaitedREADY excludes a by-hand READY by name. Bounding how long a person takes is a bound on the awaiting_merge phase, not on an outbox row.

outcome.scope: A pull request a person merges by hand is explicitly outside this issue: nothing tells the architect that nobody has merged it. Covering it needs a bound on the awaiting_merge phase and belongs in its own issue.
